chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'If a man has a slave girl for his son, is it permissible for him to sleep with her?' He said, 'He appraises her for himself with a price, and bears witness upon himself for her price; this is more beloved to me.'

key_terms.يَطَأَهَا: To sleep with / consummate relations with

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for a father to have relations with his son's slave girl according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a father having sexual relations with his son's slave girl, a common scenario in early Islamic society where property rights were distinct. Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) prescribes a specific legal procedure—appraising the girl, paying her value to the son, and bearing witness—to ensure the transaction is valid and the father's right is clearly established, preventing disputes over ownership. This emphasizes the importance of formalizing private property transfers within the family structure to legitimize the act of *tamalluk* (possession).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umer, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man, there happens to be a slave girl for his son, it is for him that he sleeps with her?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would evaluate her upon himself with a price, and he would bear witness upon him with her price. It would be more beloved to me’.
